title: Leg Nerve Injuries — Femoral, Sciatic, Fibular, Tibial and Gluteal

hook.en: A foot that slaps, a knee that gives way on stairs, a pelvis that drops when you walk — each one belongs to a different nerve. Learn the picture, the quick test and the usual site of injury.
hook.ur: Foot jo thap thap kare, knee jo seerhiyon par jawab de de, pelvis jo chalte hue gir jaye — har ek ka alag nerve hai. Tasveer, tez test aur injury ki aam jagah seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll match each leg nerve to its classic sign (foot drop, knee buckling, Trendelenburg, claw toes), test it quickly and name where it is usually injured.
goal.ur: End tak aap har leg nerve ko uske classic sign (foot drop, knee buckling, Trendelenburg, claw toes) se match karenge, jaldi test karenge aur batayenge ke aam taur par kahan zakhmi hoti hai.

text.en: The leg has fewer famous nerves than the arm, but each one has a very clear job. **Femoral** (L2–L4) straightens the knee. **Obturator** (L2–L4) squeezes the thighs together. **Superior gluteal** (L4–S1) keeps the pelvis level. **Sciatic** (L4–S3) splits into the **tibial** (plantarflexion, sole) and **common fibular** (dorsiflexion, eversion). Learn the job and the failure is obvious.
text.ur: Taang mein arm se kam mashhoor nerves hain, lekin har ek ka kaam bilkul saaf hai. **Femoral** (L2–L4) knee ko seedha karti hai. **Obturator** (L2–L4) thighs ko aapas mein milati hai. **Superior gluteal** (L4–S1) pelvis ko level rakhti hai. **Sciatic** (L4–S3) **tibial** (plantarflexion, sole) aur **common fibular** (dorsiflexion, eversion) mein baant jati hai. Kaam seekh lein to kharabi saaf nazar aati hai.

text.en: The sciatic nerve is one cable that splits into two wires at the back of the knee. The tibial wire pushes the pedal down (plantarflexion); the fibular wire lifts the foot up (dorsiflexion). Cut the fibular wire and the foot hangs and slaps; cut the tibial wire and you cannot push off.
text.ur: Sciatic nerve ek cable hai jo knee ke peechay do taaron mein baant jati hai. Tibial taar pedal neeche dabata hai (plantarflexion); fibular taar foot ko upar uthata hai (dorsiflexion). Fibular taar kat jaye to foot latakta aur thap thap karta hai; tibial taar kat jaye to aap push-off nahi kar sakte.

intro.en: Follow the nerve as it **wraps round the neck of the fibula**, where crossed legs, a tight cast or a plaster slab can press on it. The loop shows the healthy foot lifting, then **foot drop** with a high-stepping gait.
intro.ur: Nerve ko **fibula ki neck ke gird lipte** hue follow karein, jahan taang par taang rakhna, tight cast ya plaster dabao daal sakta hai. Loop pehle healthy foot ko upar uthta dikhata hai, phir **foot drop** aur uncha qadam uthane wali gait.

question.en: A woman has a new foot drop after a long hospital stay with her legs crossed in bed. Dorsiflexion and eversion are weak, but inversion and hip abduction are normal, with numbness over the top of the foot and outer shin. Which nerve?
question.ur: Hospital mein lambay arsay tak bistar mein taang par taang rakhne ke baad khatoon ko naya foot drop hai. Dorsiflexion aur eversion kamzor hain, lekin inversion aur hip abduction normal hain, aur foot ka top aur outer shin sunn hai. Kaun si nerve?

text.en: Common fibular nerve at the fibular neck
text.ur: Fibular neck par common fibular nerve

feedback.en: Yes — normal inversion and hip abduction rule out the L5 root. Remove the pressure, protect with an ankle-foot orthosis if needed and reassess.
feedback.ur: Haan — normal inversion aur hip abduction L5 root ko rule out karte hain. Dabao hatayein, zaroorat ho to ankle-foot orthosis se hifazat karein aur dobara assess karein.

feedback.en: L5 would also weaken inversion (tibialis posterior) and hip abduction (gluteus medius).
feedback.ur: L5 inversion (tibialis posterior) aur hip abduction (gluteus medius) ko bhi kamzor karti.

feedback.en: The tibial nerve causes weak plantarflexion and a numb sole, not foot drop.
feedback.ur: Tibial nerve plantarflexion kamzor aur sole sunn karti hai, foot drop nahi.

intro.en: Follow the femoral nerve under the **inguinal ligament** into the thigh. The healthy knee extends against gravity (quadriceps); the injured knee cannot straighten and gives way on stairs.
intro.ur: Femoral nerve ko **inguinal ligament** ke neeche thigh mein follow karein. Healthy knee gravity ke khilaf extend hota hai (quadriceps); injured knee seedha nahi hota aur seerhiyon par jawab de deta hai.

intro.en: Follow the nerve above **piriformis** into gluteus medius. The injured half shows the **Trendelenburg sign**: standing on the weak side, the pelvis drops on the opposite side.
intro.ur: Nerve ko **piriformis** ke upar gluteus medius tak follow karein. Injured hissa **Trendelenburg sign** dikhata hai: kamzor side par khare hone par pelvis doosri side par gir jata hai.

rows.en: Knee buckling, lost knee jerk, numb front and inner thigh and shin (saphenous)
rows.ur: Knee jawab de deta hai, knee jerk gayab, thigh ke samne aur andar aur shin sunn (saphenous)

rows.en: Under the inguinal ligament: pelvic haematoma, hip surgery, anticoagulants
rows.ur: Inguinal ligament ke neeche: pelvic haematoma, hip surgery, anticoagulants

rows.en: Weak hip adduction, wide-based gait, numb inner thigh
rows.ur: Hip adduction kamzor, wide-based gait, inner thigh sunn

rows.en: Trendelenburg sign (pelvis drops on the opposite side)
rows.ur: Trendelenburg sign (pelvis doosri side gir jata hai)

rows.en: Above piriformis: deep gluteal injections, hip surgery
rows.ur: Piriformis ke upar: deep gluteal injections, hip surgery

rows.en: FOOT DROP, steppage gait, numb dorsum of the foot and outer shin
rows.ur: FOOT DROP, steppage gait, foot ka dorsum aur outer shin sunn

rows.en: Fibular neck: crossed legs, casts, tight splints, knee dislocation
rows.ur: Fibular neck: taang par taang, casts, tight splints, knee dislocation

rows.en: Cannot rise on toes, numb sole, claw toes
rows.ur: Toes par nahi uth sakta, sole sunn, claw toes

rows.en: Tarsal tunnel behind the medial malleolus
rows.ur: Medial malleolus ke peechay tarsal tunnel

text.en: **Meralgia paraesthetica is not weakness.** The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (L2–L3) is *purely sensory*: burning, tingling or numbness on the outer thigh with **no weakness and normal reflexes**. Tight belts, obesity, pregnancy and long standing compress it under the inguinal ligament. Do not chase a disc when strength and reflexes are normal and the patch is exactly the outer thigh.
text.ur: **Meralgia paraesthetica kamzori nahi hai.** Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (L2–L3) *sirf sensory* hai: outer thigh par jalan, jhunjhunahat ya numbness, **kamzori nahi aur reflexes normal**. Tang belt, obesity, pregnancy aur der tak khara rehna isay inguinal ligament ke neeche dabate hain. Jab taqat aur reflexes normal hon aur patch bilkul outer thigh ho to disc ke peechay na bhagein.

intro.en: Follow the sciatic nerve from the **greater sciatic notch**, deep to piriformis, down the thigh and see it split above the knee. Hamstrings and everything below the knee depend on it.
intro.ur: Sciatic nerve ko **greater sciatic notch** se, piriformis ke neeche, thigh mein neeche aur knee ke upar baantte hue follow karein. Hamstrings aur knee ke neeche sab kuch isi par depend karta hai.

question.en: A patient cannot stand on tiptoe on the left leg and has a numb sole. Which nerve division is mainly affected?
question.ur: Patient left taang par tiptoe par khara nahi ho sakta aur sole sunn hai. Kaun sa nerve division zyada affected hai?

feedback.en: Yes — plantarflexion and the plantar skin both depend on the tibial nerve.
feedback.ur: Haan — plantarflexion aur plantar skin dono tibial nerve par depend karti hain.
Yeh dorsiflexion aur eversion ko affect karti hai.
Yeh knee extension ko affect karti hai.

text.en: **Orthoses and walking.** For foot drop use an ankle-foot orthosis (or a functional electrical stimulator) so the toes clear the floor, and teach a safe stair strategy. For femoral weakness a knee brace or a locked knee gait helps while the quadriceps recovers, and for Trendelenburg a cane in the hand opposite the weak hip reduces the load on the abductors. Nerve recovery is about 1 mm per day, so monitor strength and sensation every few weeks.
text.ur: **Orthoses aur chalna.** Foot drop ke liye ankle-foot orthosis (ya functional electrical stimulator) use karein taake toes zameen se uthein, aur seerhiyon ki mehfooz strategy sikhayein. Femoral kamzori mein knee brace ya locked knee gait madad deti hai jab tak quadriceps theek ho, aur Trendelenburg mein kamzor hip ki opposite haath mein chhari abductors par bojh kam karti hai. Nerve recovery takriban 1 mm roz hai, is liye har chand haftay taqat aur sensation monitor karein.

question.en: Why does a deep gluteal injection or hip surgery sometimes cause foot drop and a drop in the pelvis in the same patient?
question.ur: Deep gluteal injection ya hip surgery kabhi kabhi ek hi patient mein foot drop aur pelvis ka girna kyun karti hai?

answer.en: Because both the **sciatic nerve** (its fibular part is more exposed and easily hurt) and the **superior gluteal nerve** run close to the hip joint and piriformis. An injury near the greater sciatic notch can affect either or both. Always test hip abduction and plantarflexion as well as dorsiflexion.
answer.ur: Kyunke **sciatic nerve** (iska fibular hissa zyada exposed hai aur asani se zakhmi hota hai) aur **superior gluteal nerve** dono hip joint aur piriformis ke qareeb se guzarti hain. Greater sciatic notch ke qareeb chot kisi ek ya dono ko affect kar sakti hai. Dorsiflexion ke saath hip abduction aur plantarflexion bhi hamesha test karein.

question.en: Standing on the right leg, a patient's left pelvis drops. Which structure is weak?
question.ur: Right taang par khare hone par patient ka left pelvis gir jata hai. Kaun sa structure kamzor hai?

text.en: Right gluteus medius (superior gluteal nerve or L5 root)
text.ur: Right gluteus medius (superior gluteal nerve ya L5 root)

feedback.en: Yes — the stance-side abductors hold the pelvis level; when they fail the opposite side drops.
feedback.ur: Haan — stance side ke abductors pelvis ko level rakhte hain; woh fail hon to opposite side gir jati hai.

feedback.en: The weak muscle is on the **stance** side, not the side that drops.
feedback.ur: Kamzor muscle **stance** side par hota hai, us par nahi jo girti hai.

feedback.en: Quadriceps weakness makes the knee buckle; it does not tilt the pelvis.
feedback.ur: Quadriceps ki kamzori knee ko jawab dilati hai; pelvis ko tilt nahi karti.

text.en: **Refer urgently** for foot drop with severe back or leg pain or bladder or bowel changes (cauda equina), a cold or pulseless leg, a rapidly enlarging thigh swelling on blood thinners (retroperitoneal or thigh haematoma compressing the femoral nerve), or a new deficit after surgery or trauma.
text.ur: **Foran refer karein** agar foot drop ke saath shadeed kamar ya taang ka dard ya bladder aur bowel ki tabdeeli ho (cauda equina), thandi ya bina pulse wali taang ho, blood thinners par thigh ki tezi se barhti soojan ho (retroperitoneal ya thigh haematoma jo femoral nerve ko dabata hai), ya surgery ya trauma ke baad nayi kami ho.

summary.en: Know the job of each leg nerve: femoral straightens the knee, obturator adducts, superior gluteal levels the pelvis, tibial plantarflexes, common fibular dorsiflexes.
summary.ur: Har leg nerve ka kaam jaanein: femoral knee seedha karti hai, obturator adduct karti hai, superior gluteal pelvis level karti hai, tibial plantarflex, common fibular dorsiflex.

summary.en: Match the picture: foot drop and steppage = common fibular, Trendelenburg = superior gluteal, buckling = femoral, no push-off = tibial.
summary.ur: Tasveer match karein: foot drop aur steppage = common fibular, Trendelenburg = superior gluteal, buckling = femoral, push-off nahi = tibial.

summary.en: Test muscles that share the root but not the nerve to separate nerve from root; protect with orthoses and refer sudden or traumatic deficits.
summary.ur: Nerve ko root se alag karne ke liye aise muscles test karein jo root share karen magar nerve nahi; orthoses se hifazat karein aur achanak ya trauma wali kami ko refer karein.

front.en: What is the sign of a common fibular nerve palsy?
front.ur: Common fibular nerve palsy ka sign?

back.en: Foot drop with a steppage gait and numbness over the dorsum of the foot and outer shin.
back.ur: Foot drop, steppage gait aur foot ke dorsum aur outer shin ki numbness.

back.en: The pelvis drops on the side opposite the stance leg, because the stance-side gluteus medius (superior gluteal nerve) is weak.
back.ur: Pelvis stance leg ki opposite side gir jata hai, kyunke stance side ka gluteus medius (superior gluteal nerve) kamzor hai.

front.en: Which nerve causes the knee to give way on stairs?
front.ur: Seerhiyon par knee ko kaun si nerve jawab dilati hai?

back.en: The femoral nerve (quadriceps weakness), with a lost knee jerk and numb front of the thigh.
back.ur: Femoral nerve (quadriceps ki kamzori), knee jerk gayab aur thigh ka samna sunn.

back.en: Compression of the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve under the inguinal ligament: burning or numb outer thigh with no weakness.
back.ur: Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve ka inguinal ligament ke neeche dabna: outer thigh par jalan ya numbness, kamzori nahi.

note.en: Follow each leg nerve in 3D and compare healthy with injured.
note.ur: Har leg nerve 3D mein follow karein aur healthy ko injured se compare karein.

note.en: Separate nerve lesions from root lesions.
note.ur: Nerve lesions ko root lesions se alag karein.
